priorityqueue-priority-order-not-stable.title: Add an explicit tie-breaker when PriorityQueue order must be stable
priorityqueue-priority-order-not-stable.short: Equal priorities do not define FIFO ordering
priorityqueue-priority-order-not-stable.summary: PriorityQueue orders elements by priority, but equal-priority elements should not be assumed to dequeue in insertion order.
priorityqueue-priority-order-not-stable.why: Code that silently depends on FIFO behavior for ties can change behavior as heap operations rearrange equal-priority entries.
priorityqueue-priority-order-not-stable.tips: Include a monotonic sequence or another deterministic secondary key in the priority when stable tie ordering matters.

random-shared-concurrent-randomness.title: Use Random.Shared for ordinary concurrent random values
random-shared-concurrent-randomness.short: Avoid repeatedly constructing Random instances on hot concurrent paths
random-shared-concurrent-randomness.summary: Random.Shared provides a process-wide Random instance designed for convenient concurrent use in ordinary non-cryptographic scenarios.
random-shared-concurrent-randomness.why: Creating many short-lived Random objects adds overhead and ad-hoc synchronization around a shared Random complicates otherwise simple code.
random-shared-concurrent-randomness.tips: Use Random.Shared for simulation, jitter, and similar non-security uses; use a cryptographic generator when unpredictability is a security requirement.

activitylistener-sampling-boundary.title: Control tracing cost at the ActivityListener sampling boundary
activitylistener-sampling-boundary.short: Decide which activities collect data before doing expensive enrichment
activitylistener-sampling-boundary.summary: ActivityListener chooses which ActivitySource instances to observe and how much data newly created activities should record.
activitylistener-sampling-boundary.why: Recording every trace with full data can create unnecessary allocation and export volume on high-throughput paths.
activitylistener-sampling-boundary.tips: Sample according to observability needs and avoid expensive tags or payload construction when the activity is not recording them.

exception-data-structured-context-bounda.title: Attach small structured context to exceptions deliberately
exception-data-structured-context-bounda.short: Exception.Data can carry diagnostic values across a throw boundary
exception-data-structured-context-bounda.summary: Exception.Data can associate small contextual values with an exception when creating a custom exception type would be excessive.
exception-data-structured-context-bounda.why: Embedding every diagnostic value into a message makes structured logging harder, while putting large or sensitive objects into Data creates different problems.
exception-data-structured-context-bounda.tips: Use stable keys and small non-sensitive values, and prefer dedicated exception properties when the data is part of a public exception contract.

tcpclient-stream-framing-boundary.title: Define message framing explicitly on TCP streams
tcpclient-stream-framing-boundary.short: TCP preserves bytes, not application message boundaries
tcpclient-stream-framing-boundary.summary: TCP exposes an ordered byte stream, so one send does not imply one matching receive and application messages need their own framing rule.
tcpclient-stream-framing-boundary.why: Assuming each read returns one complete message fails under fragmentation, buffering, coalescing, or short reads.
tcpclient-stream-framing-boundary.tips: Use a length prefix, delimiter, or fixed-size protocol and loop until the required bytes for each frame have actually arrived.

stream-copy-buffer-ownership.title: Make buffer ownership explicit in custom stream copy loops
stream-copy-buffer-ownership.short: Reusable buffers need a clear renter, user, and return point
stream-copy-buffer-ownership.summary: Custom stream-copy loops can reuse pooled buffers to reduce allocation, but the buffer lifetime must cover every asynchronous operation that uses it.
stream-copy-buffer-ownership.why: Returning a pooled array while an async read or write still references it can corrupt data, while never returning it defeats pooling.
stream-copy-buffer-ownership.tips: Keep one clear owner around the full copy loop, await all buffer users before returning it, and clear sensitive contents when necessary.

reflection-open-generic-construction.title: Close open generic types before runtime construction
reflection-open-generic-construction.short: Generic type definitions are templates rather than constructible runtime types
reflection-open-generic-construction.summary: Reflection can inspect open generic definitions and create closed constructed types by supplying concrete type arguments.
reflection-open-generic-construction.why: Trying to instantiate a type that still contains unbound generic parameters fails because its runtime layout and contracts are not fully specified.
reflection-open-generic-construction.tips: Check ContainsGenericParameters, validate constraints, then use MakeGenericType only with type arguments that satisfy the generic definition.

aspnetcore-cancellationtoken-endpoint-bi.title: Bind ASP.NET Core endpoint cancellation and pass it downstream
aspnetcore-cancellationtoken-endpoint-bi.short: Use the endpoint CancellationToken for request-scoped work
aspnetcore-cancellationtoken-endpoint-bi.summary: Minimal API endpoints can bind a CancellationToken representing request cancellation and pass it to database, network, and other cancellable operations.
aspnetcore-cancellationtoken-endpoint-bi.why: Accepting request cancellation at the HTTP boundary but dropping it before downstream calls leaves expensive work running after the result is no longer needed.
aspnetcore-cancellationtoken-endpoint-bi.tips: Accept CancellationToken in the endpoint signature and propagate the same request-scoped token through cancellable service calls.

unity-profiler-marker-hot-path-instrumen.title: Instrument Unity hot paths with reusable ProfilerMarker instances
unity-profiler-marker-hot-path-instrumen.short: Add targeted profiler scopes without per-frame marker construction
unity-profiler-marker-hot-path-instrumen.summary: ProfilerMarker lets Unity code expose meaningful custom regions in profiling data so expensive application-specific work can be located precisely.
unity-profiler-marker-hot-path-instrumen.why: A frame-time spike hidden inside a broad Update sample is difficult to attribute, while creating instrumentation objects repeatedly can itself add noise.
unity-profiler-marker-hot-path-instrumen.tips: Keep markers static or otherwise reusable and place scopes around meaningful units of work rather than every tiny operation.

async-dispose-await-using-lifetime.title: Use await using for resources with asynchronous cleanup
async-dispose-await-using-lifetime.short: Keep IAsyncDisposable cleanup inside the asynchronous lifetime
async-dispose-await-using-lifetime.summary: await using ensures DisposeAsync is awaited when leaving scope, which is useful when cleanup itself needs asynchronous I/O or flushing.
async-dispose-await-using-lifetime.why: Calling asynchronous cleanup without awaiting it can let the method finish before resources are fully released or persisted.
async-dispose-await-using-lifetime.tips: Use await using when the resource implements IAsyncDisposable and keep the scope aligned with the last operation that needs the resource.
